03 Receiver Personas

Three receivers, three different relationships with money.

Persona 01

Personal Needs

Receives weekly to cover groceries, school fees and medicine. Money lands and is spent.

Persona 02

Dream Builders

Saves on behalf of senders towards bigger goals — a home, a small business — with incentives along the way.

Persona 03

Community Receivers

Cashes out and distributes — neighbours, elders, friends. Returns home with only a small token.

04 Tensions in the Journey

What pushes them away — what pulls them in.

Forces shape the experience in equal measure.

Drivers

Forces that shape the experience

Proximity

A nearby outlet beats almost everything else.

Predictability

Consistent rules. Money guaranteed when promised.

Safety

Protection from scams, theft & staff negligence.

Respect

Dignity — especially for elderly & Indigenous receivers.

Barriers

Forces that shape the experience

Counter friction

Long queues, unclear rules, dismissive staff.

Forced purchases

Pressure to buy something when cashing out is resented.

Crime & safety

Receivers hide cash, vary pickup times — take extra precautions.

Banking distrust

Hidden charges, scams & stolen funds stories keep them out.

05 Cultural Backdrop

Why this corridor still runs on cash.

Banking is growing in Mexico, but cash remains how this corridor breathes. Four reasons surfaced again and again.

Tradition & sharing

Tangible, familiar, easy to divide across family and community.

Safety & control

People feel more in charge and safer when they hold money in hand.

Mistrust of banks

Stories circulate about hidden fees, "stolen" funds, suspicions of collusion with crime.

Fear of exposure

Un-documented senders often avoid banks to reduce risk of detection.

07 Experience Pillars

Five pillars to build trust.

The lens from which every design decision is taken and tested against.

01

Keep it Simple & Flexible

Reduce cognitive load at every step. The service should adapt to varying levels of digital literacy — from first-time senders to habitual users — without added friction.

02

Honor Familiarity

Build on existing habits and trusted anchors — cash, known stores, familiar language. Don't replace what already works; enhance it.

03

Enable Predictability & Control

Give users clear, consistent information at every stage. Predictable fees, reliable timelines, and visible status build the confidence to return.

04

Deliver Maximum Value

Every transaction should feel worth it — competitive rates, rewards, and ancillary benefits that make the service a net positive beyond the transfer itself.

05

Build Transparency & Trust

Surface what is usually hidden — fees, exchange rates, processing steps — so users feel respected, not managed. Trust is earned through radical clarity.

09 Design Outcome

Inside the app people already trust.

The pillars have shaped a new remittance experience that is familiar and people can rely on.

One known environment

Money transfers within a platform they already trust.

Familiar at every step

The flow mirrors patterns users already know — same language, same gestures, same structure. Nothing to relearn, no moment of hesitation.

Cash-friendly by default

Pick up at 3,000+ store locations customers already shop at.

Transparency upfront

Exchange rate & total receivable shown before the sender commits.

10 Final UI Screens

Two flows, one app.

Designed end-to-end experience backed by the experience pillars — the sender's app in the US and the receiver's app in Mexico share a vocabulary, a tone, and a sense of certainty.

Sender · US
PL
Persona · Sender Pablo Lopez · United States Sends $300–500 every two weeks to family in Mexico. Wants reassurance the money is moving, and a reason to come back.
Step 01

Nudge for repeat sender on home page

For users who send money to their family regularly, we can nudge them during the time they usually transact.

Step 02

Transfer details

Based on their previous preferences and details — all information has been pre-filled.

Step 03

Review details

One final check, ensuring everything is right and their loved one will receive the correct amount.

Step 04

Tracking and confirmation

Senders can track the entire process from their end till cash is collected — keeping their minds at peace.

Receiver · MX
EG
Persona · Receiver Emilia Garcia · Mexico Picks up cash for her household. Wants clarity on when, where and how — without a queue or a hidden fee.
Step 01

Instant updates

Receiver gets instant updates when the transfer is initiated, via their preferred communication channels.

Step 02

Details & tracking

They instantly have access to live tracking and all details.

Step 03

Digital KYC

Receiver can complete their KYC online by verifying their ID, making the process at the store faster.

Step 04

QR code & pickup details

With KYC completed, they just show the QR code at the store counter to receive cash. We suggest their nearest store, with options to change it.
